A II∞ factor combines factoriality, type II, and infinite identity; the finite-projection supply and semifinite trace distinguish it from type III and II₁.
A II₁ factor is type II with finite identity, equivalently finite with trivial center; the exclusion of finite-dimensional matrix factors and normalized trace are correct.
Type II combines semifiniteness with absence of nonzero abelian projections and applies to general algebras; finite projections/traces and the type-I/III distinctions are accurately qualified.
A type III factor is simultaneously a von Neumann factor and type III algebra, hence has no nonzero finite projections; the factor and type conditions are separately stated.

The σ-strong topology on B(H) uses square-summable Hilbert-space sequences in the displayed ℓ² seminorm; restriction to concrete von Neumann algebras is correctly described.

Unitality is existence of a two-sided identity in a C*-algebra; the source correctly treats norm/positivity and approximate identities, unitization, and unital morphisms as consequences or additions.
A unital *-homomorphism is a structure-preserving map between unital C*-algebras carrying 1A to 1B; the extra identity condition is clearly separated from *-homomorphism.

For nonunital A, A⊕C with the displayed operations and canonical C*-norm is the minimal unitization; A is an essential ideal and the universal unital extension property is correct.
Given generators, relations, and a chosen unital/nonunital C*-category, the universal object has unique *-homomorphisms to every realization and is unique up to generator-preserving isomorphism.

A factor is a von Neumann algebra with scalar center, equivalently only trivial central projections; the definition correctly captures absence of central direct-sum decomposition.
